$schema: internal build sheet, not a Railway file
name: Rakazo

upstream.$note: Pinned to the v0.1.6 image tag, not edge: edge moves on every main build and a template must not silently change under existing deployers.

image.$note: Thin wrapper over ghcr.io/elie222/rakazo/app:v0.1.6. Two reasons upstream's image alone cannot deploy on Railway: (1) Railway volumes mount root-owned and upstream runs as uid 1000, so /data (agent homes, artifacts, push tokens, Pi sessions) is EACCES; (2) api and worker share DATA_DIR and Railway volumes attach to one service only, so api+worker+web must run in one container, which needs a multi-process boot upstream's CMD does not have. Wrapper = USER root entrypoint that chowns /data then runuser-drops to node and boots all three processes with wait -n.

topology.decision: Two services: Railway Postgres, and one app container running api + worker + web (vite preview).
why_bundled: apps/api and apps/worker both hold bot state under DATA_DIR (LocalAgentHomeStore, LocalArtifactStore, Pi session roots, Expo push tokens - verified in apps/api/src/app.ts and apps/worker/src/index.ts). A Railway volume cannot attach to two services, so they share one container and one /data volume.

web is bundled too rather than split: vite preview already same-origin-proxies /api and /rpc to API_PROXY_TARGET (default 127.0.0.1:3100), so in one container no private networking is involved at all and the IPv6 question shrinks to the single public listener.
api binds loopback (API_HOST unset, default 127.0.0.1) and is only reachable through the web proxy, matching upstream's published-images Compose which never exposes :3100 publicly.
topology.sandbox: SANDBOX_PROVIDER defaults to none. The docker provider is impossible on Railway (no docker socket, no sibling containers); deployers wanting bot computers set e2b, daytona or box plus the matching API key. Supervisor service and SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN are deliberately absent - the token only guards the docker-socket supervisor.
topology.alternative_rejected: Faithful compose-mirroring split (api, worker, web as separate services) silently breaks bot file state because the volume cannot be shared. A web-only split saves nothing and adds an IPv6 private-network hop.

services.name: Postgres
services.$note: Railway's own Postgres config shape, lettertrace precedent. PGDATA is a SUBDIRECTORY of the mount because volume roots contain lost+found and initdb refuses a non-empty directory.

services.name: Rakazo
services.$note_start_command: Deliberately empty. Railway execs a start command raw and DISCARDS the image entrypoint; the entrypoint is where the /data chown and the whole boot sequence live.

healthcheck.$note: Unauthenticated 200 served by the api THROUGH the vite proxy, so a pass proves web + proxy + api + migrations all at once. /health exists only on the api's loopback port and is not proxied. No hyphens in the path (Railway rejects those silently).

domain.$note: Pinned. Railway's port autodetection is unreliable and the injected PORT=8080 would drift the healthcheck off the real listener.

PORT.$note: Railway injects PORT=8080 on image services and healthchecks against PORT; pin it to the port the domain targets. boot.sh passes --port "${PORT:-5173}".

DATABASE_URL.$note: Name-based reference, never a service UUID: UUID-keyed references resolve to empty after config regeneration.

BETTER_AUTH_SECRET.$note: 32+ chars required by upstream env docs.

ENCRYPTION_KEY.$note: Exactly 64 hex chars (encrypts stored provider credentials). Changing it makes saved keys unreadable - never regenerate on an existing deployment.

SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET.$note: Guards the noVNC screen proxy; unused while SANDBOX_PROVIDER=none but cheap to provision.

RAKAZO_HOST.$note: vite preview allowedHosts is exactly [RAKAZO_HOST]; without the public hostname every browser request is 403 Blocked.

SIGNUPS_ENABLED.$note: First registered user becomes the deployment owner. Deployers wanting a private instance set SIGNUP_ALLOWLIST or flip this to false after registering.

SANDBOX_PROVIDER.$note: none | e2b | daytona | box. docker is not possible on Railway. none = bots chat but cannot open a computer.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY.$note: Deployment-wide fallback model. Optional: models can also be connected in the UI after signup, which is where the app verifies keys anyway. PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER stays openrouter to match.

$note_prompts: Four prompts, three of them skippable: SANDBOX_PROVIDER (default none), one provider key, and an optional OpenRouter key. No account signup blocks the deploy button.
telemetry: PostHog keys unset by default. Nothing leaves the deployment except calls to providers the deployer configures with the deployer's own keys.
